title: Containerization and Orchestration: A Small Lab You Can Run

cover.alt: Conceptual exploded view of a small application packaged into a container and connected to a response check.

figures.title: Four files, four responsibilities
figures.summary: Each artifact in the lab has one job in the path from source code to a running service.

items.label: index.js
items.detail: Defines the HTTP service and its health endpoint.

items.label: package.json
items.detail: Declares dependencies and the start command.

items.label: Dockerfile
items.detail: Packages the application and its runtime into an image.

items.label: Compose file
items.detail: Defines how to build and run the service with a mapped port.

figures.caption: A file map of the small lab shown in the article; no cluster is required for this example.

figures.title: Separate the artifact from the running proof
figures.summary: Building an image and receiving a response are different checks.

items.label: Run locally
items.detail: Confirm the health route responds before packaging.

items.label: Build the image
items.detail: Create the container artifact from the Dockerfile.

items.label: Start with Compose
items.detail: Run that artifact through the repeatable configuration.

items.label: Request health
items.detail: Call the mapped endpoint and inspect its response.

items.label: Stop the lab
items.detail: End the running session when the check is complete.

figures.caption: The verification sequence in this post. A running process alone is not the health-response check.
